edges.description: Deficiency of the translation-regulating factor reduces production of COX1.
Reduced COX1 supply and defective coordination of early assembly restrict mature complex IV formation.
Deficient holoenzyme abundance reduces complex IV catalytic capacity.
Impaired oxidative metabolism is a plausible contributor to the severe lactic acidosis, but the intermediate flux changes were not directly measured in the infant.
Cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction provides a mechanistic explanation for the reported cardiomyopathy; the intervening developmental and metabolic steps remain unresolved.
Respiratory dysfunction may contribute to the observed white-matter injury, but its cellular sequence is unresolved.
The COX14 knock-in mouse links respiratory deficiency to increased oxidant production in hepatocytes; this branch has not been demonstrated in patients.
Antioxidant rescue supports ROS-dependent mitochondrial RNA release. The specific membrane pore or transport route has not been resolved.
Cytosolic mitochondrial RNA is implicated in RIG-I/MDA5-associated inflammatory signaling in mutant mouse liver.
Persistent innate signaling is implicated in liver injury in the mouse model; contribution to the human neonatal course remains untested.
Patient cells show reduced mature complex IV.
edges.limitations: Residual fibroblast activity does not predict neonatal tissue severity.
